items.title: onehumanbeing/esp32-iphone-agent
items.why: It demonstrates a creative and affordable way to build hardware-controlled AI agents using basic components.
items.summary: This open-source project uses a low-cost $7 ESP32 microcontroller to let AI vision models perceive an iPhone screen and interact with it using touch controls.

items.title: outcrawlai/scout
items.why: It is a practical open-source browser agent tool you can inspect and use for web automation.
items.summary: Scout is an open-source browser agent that automates web navigation and online tasks using AI.

items.title: chenglou/handwired
items.why: It is an intriguing open-source project bridging web development in JavaScript with fundamental machine learning concepts.
items.summary: Handwired is an experimental open-source library that transforms standard JavaScript functions into neural network models.

items.title: Llama.cpp on a jailbroken PS5: run any GGUF model natively on the console
items.why: It is an impressive example of running open-source AI models on everyday consumer hardware.
items.summary: Developers ported llama.cpp to jailbroken PS5 consoles, allowing open-source language models to run locally using the console graphics hardware.

items.title: What this bankruptcy says about AI startups
items.why: It helps you understand the evolving job market and business strategies inside the AI startup ecosystem.
items.summary: This analysis explains how big tech firms acquire AI startups by licensing technology and hiring founders rather than completing traditional buyouts.

items.title: Postgres 19 delayed after AI reviewers find more bugs than humans can fix
items.why: It illustrates a practical dilemma software teams face when integrating AI code review tools into real projects.
items.summary: Development on Postgres 19 was delayed because automated AI code reviewers flagged more potential bugs than human maintainers could inspect and fix.

items.title: 90% of US working hours are spent on tasks not covered well by AI benchmarks
items.why: It gives you realistic context on how current AI models perform relative to real-world human jobs.
items.summary: A recent discussion highlights that 90% of actual workplace tasks are not adequately measured by current AI benchmark tests.

items.title: Claude reveals ECDSA curve origins
items.why: It highlights how modern LLMs can assist in solving real-world mathematical and technical puzzles.
items.summary: Security researchers used Claude to analyze mathematical patterns, solving a long-standing mystery behind key cryptographic seed values.

items.title: Anthropic assigned highest junk credit rating in June
items.why: It offers insight into the financial realities and business challenges facing major AI companies.
items.summary: Credit rating agencies assigned AI startup Anthropic a junk credit rating, drawing attention to high operating costs and financial burn rates.

items.title: Inside Ukrainian offensive pushing Russia back - with Starlink playing a key role
items.why: It keeps you informed on major global news and shows how technology like satellite internet impacts real-world events.
items.summary: Ukrainian military forces report making progress in Donbas while relying heavily on SpaceX Starlink terminals for tactical communications.

items.title: Iran war live: Trump claims US Navy blockade stops Iranian ships in Hormuz
items.why: It covers a critical world news story involving major international conflict and shipping routes.
items.summary: U.S. officials report establishing a naval blockade in the Strait of Hormuz to stop Iranian shipping traffic amid rising regional tensions.
